evals.prompt: Review the database schema of the repo in evals/files/sample-repo before we go live. We use EF Core on SQL Server plus a few hand-written SQL scripts under db/. Tell me what is wrong with the tables and indexes and whether our migrations can be rolled back.
evals.expected_output: A report with a table-by-table checklist covering Products, Orders, OrderLines, Users, Customers, Payments, AuditLogs and shipments; findings (DB- prefix) for: AuditLogs has no primary key (High), Payments.Amount and OrderLine.UnitPrice/LineTotal use float/double for money (Critical), Payments.OrderId and OrderLine.ProductId are unindexed FK/FK-like columns (High, one finding with both locations or two findings), migration AddCustomerNotes has an empty Down() (High), plus lower findings for nvarchar(max)/naive DateTime and the hard Remove() in OrderManager despite IsDeleted. Products, Users, Customers and AddDiscount are not flagged. Recommended-index table cites OrderManager.LinesForProduct for OrderLines.ProductId and the FK join for Payments.OrderId. Migration report lists InitialCreate (initial), AddCustomerNotes (no), AddDiscount (yes), knex 20260301_create_shipments (no).
expectations: Output contains a finding about AuditLogs lacking a primary key
Output contains a Critical finding about money stored as float/double naming Payments.Amount or OrderLine.UnitPrice
Output contains a finding about an unindexed foreign key naming Payments.OrderId or OrderLine.ProductId
Output contains a finding that migration AddCustomerNotes has an empty Down() / cannot be rolled back
Output does not flag Products, Users, Customers, or the AddDiscount migration as defects
Report includes a table-by-table checklist, a recommended indexes table with justifying queries, and a migration reversibility table
Finding ids start with DB- and findings.json validates with ../audit-finding-writer/scripts/findings.py validate
Report lists what was not checked (for example live index usage statistics)

evals.prompt: Our sales list page is slow and someone said it's a missing index. Can you look at the schema in evals/files/sample-repo and tell me which indexes we should add and why?
evals.expected_output: Runs schema_checklist.py, produces a recommended-index list: OrderLines (ProductId) or (CompanyId, ProductId) justified by OrderManager.LinesForProduct; Payments (OrderId) justified by the FK join; notes that Orders already has (CompanyId, BranchId, CreatedAt) covering GetPaginationList so the slowness may be elsewhere; delegates query-plan measurement to audit-performance-and-scalability; still records the other schema defects it noticed as findings or as items for the full audit.
expectations: Recommends an index on OrderLines.ProductId citing OrderManager.LinesForProduct
Recommends an index on Payments.OrderId citing the foreign key join
States that Orders (CompanyId, BranchId, CreatedAt) already covers GetPaginationList
Mentions measuring with an execution plan or delegating to audit-performance-and-scalability
Does not recommend an index on a soft-delete flag alone

evals.prompt: Check whether the migrations in evals/files/sample-repo are reversible and whether any would lose data.
evals.expected_output: Migration reversibility report: InitialCreate reversible (initial), AddCustomerNotes irreversible (empty Down, contains raw SQL), AddDiscount reversible, knex create_shipments irreversible (no down). No data-loss steps beyond the Down() of InitialCreate/AddDiscount, which is expected. Seed.sql contains no real PII. One High finding for AddCustomerNotes and one for the Knex migration (or one finding with two locations), with remediation showing the Down()/down body to add.
expectations: Report table lists all four migrations with a reversible yes/no column
AddCustomerNotes is marked irreversible and noted as containing raw SQL
The Knex shipments migration is marked irreversible because down() is missing
AddDiscount and InitialCreate are not reported as defects
seed.sql is not flagged for PII
Remediation includes the concrete Down() body (DropColumn Notes) for AddCustomerNotes
